body.heading: Why one sentence works
paragraphs: Most journals fail because they ask for pages on days when you have nothing left. One sentence lowers the cost to almost nothing, so the habit survives busy and tired days.
The constraint is also a pleasure. Choosing the single sentence means choosing what the day was about, and that small act of choosing is the reflection itself.

body.heading: Make the sentence earn its place
paragraphs: Skip the weather report unless the weather truly mattered. Prefer the specific over the general: not 'good day with friends' but 'Mara tried to teach me chess and we laughed until our sides hurt'.
Keep the journal by your bed or with your keys, and write at the same moment each day. Missing a day is not failure; write two sentences tomorrow, or simply continue.

takeaway: One true sentence a day adds up to a year you can reread.
